missing_details: Specification that the matrix is square of order n for each positive integer n
Definition of the function D(n) giving the maximal determinant for order n
Explicit domain of matrix entries as exactly ±1
Statement that the objective is to determine D(n) for all n
Clarification that n ranges over all positive integers
refined_question: For each positive integer n, let D(n) denote the maximum value of det(A) over all n×n matrices A whose entries are each either +1 or −1. Determine D(n) for every positive integer n.
equivalent_formulation: Determine the maximum determinant of an n×n matrix with entries in {0,1}, noting that the maximal determinant for {1,−1} matrices of order n equals 2^{n−1} times the maximal determinant for {0,1} matrices of order n−1.
justification: The canonical statement on Wikipedia asks precisely for the largest determinant of a ±1 matrix, but does not make explicit the dependence on matrix order n, the definition of D(n), or that the problem asks to determine D(n) for all positive integers n. It also mentions an equivalent formulation for {0,1}-matrices, which is included here only because the source explicitly states the equivalence.
